metadata.description: Evaluation dataset for Legal RAG on Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (India)

queries.query: What is res judicata and which section defines it?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 11 defines res judicata - no Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties.

queries.query: Which courts have jurisdiction to try civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 9 states that Courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.

queries.query: What is the procedure for second appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 100 provides that a second appeal lies to the High Court from every decree passed in appeal by any Court subordinate to the High Court, if the High Court is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.

queries.query: What are the inherent powers of the Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 151 provides that nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.

queries.query: What is the power of revision under CPC?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 115 empowers the High Court to call for the record of any case decided by any Court subordinate to it and may make such order as it thinks fit, in cases where jurisdiction was exercised illegally or with material irregularity.

queries.query: What is the procedure for review of judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 114 provides that any person considering himself aggrieved by a decree or order may apply for a review of judgment to the Court which passed the decree or made the order.

queries.query: Where should a suit for immovable property be instituted?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 16 provides that suits for recovery of immovable property or for partition, foreclosure, sale, or redemption shall be instituted in the Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the property is situate.

queries.query: What is the rule regarding stay of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 10 provides that no Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties.

queries.query: What properties are exempt from attachment and sale?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 60 lists properties liable to attachment and sale, and provides exemptions including necessary wearing apparel, tools of artisans, personal ornaments of women, and certain agricultural implements.

queries.query: What is the procedure for execution of decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 51 provides that the Court may enforce execution by delivery of property, attachment and sale, arrest and detention, or appointing a receiver.

queries.query: What is the time limit for execution of decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 48 was repealed. Now under Limitation Act, execution must be applied for within 12 years from the date when the decree became enforceable.

queries.query: What is a decree and what is an order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2(2) defines decree as the formal expression of an adjudication conclusively determining the rights of the parties. Section 2(14) defines order as the formal expression of any decision of a Civil Court which is not a decree.

queries.query: What is the provision for compensatory costs?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 35A provides that if any party makes a false or vexatious claim or defence, the Court may award compensatory costs not exceeding three thousand rupees or the limits prescribed by High Court.

queries.query: What is the provision for interest on judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 34 provides that where a decree is for payment of money, the Court may order interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable from the date of the suit to the date of the decree.

queries.query: What is an interpleader suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 88 provides that where two or more persons claim adversely to one another the same debt or property from a person who claims no interest except for charges, such person may institute an interpleader suit.

queries.query: What is the provision for suits against Government?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 79 provides for suits by or against Government in the name of Union of India or State. Section 80 requires a two-month notice before instituting suit against Government.

queries.query: What is the power of Court to issue commissions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 75 empowers the Court to issue commissions for examining witnesses, making local investigations, examining or adjusting accounts, making partition, or conducting sale.

queries.query: What is the provision regarding foreign judgments?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 13 lists cases when foreign judgment is not conclusive (lack of jurisdiction, not on merits, founded on incorrect view of law, etc.). Section 14 creates a presumption that foreign judgment was pronounced by a court of competent jurisdiction.

queries.query: Who can file a suit for public nuisance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 91 provides that a suit for declaration and injunction or other relief in case of public nuisance may be instituted by the Advocate-General or two or more persons with the leave of the Court.

queries.query: What is the rule about transferees and legal representatives?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 49 provides that every decree may be executed against transferee of the property. Section 50 allows execution against legal representative to the extent of property in their hands.

queries.query: What is the procedure for arrest and detention in execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 55 deals with arrest and detention of judgment debtor. Section 56 prohibits arrest of women in execution of money decree. Section 58 deals with detention and release.

queries.query: What is the provision for settlement of disputes outside Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 89 provides that the Court may refer the parties to arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement through Lok Adalat, or mediation where it appears that elements of settlement exist.

queries.query: What is the definition of mesne profits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2(12) defines mesne profits as profits which the person in wrongful possession actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received, together with interest.

queries.query: What is the power of Appellate Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 107 provides that the Appellate Court has power to determine a case finally, remand a case, frame issues and refer them for trial, take additional evidence, or do anything which ought to have been done by the lower court.

queries.query: What is a preliminary decree and final decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2(2) defines preliminary decree as one which declares rights but requires further proceedings. Final decree completely disposes of the suit. Section 97 bars appeal from final decree if no appeal from preliminary decree.

queries.query: What is the provision for reference to High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 113 provides that any Court may state a case and refer it to the High Court if it is satisfied that a question of law arises in a suit and the decision will dispose of the case.

queries.query: What is pecuniary jurisdiction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 6 provides that save as provided, any suit may be instituted in any Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the value of the subject-matter falls within the pecuniary limits.

queries.query: What is the rule for distribution of assets in execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 73 provides that proceeds of execution sale shall be rateably distributed among all decree-holders who have applied for execution and whose decrees have not been fully satisfied.

queries.query: What is the effect of attachment on private alienation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 64 provides that where attachment has been made, any private transfer or delivery of the property attached shall be void against all claims enforceable under the attachment.

queries.query: What is the provision for suits by or against minors?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXXII provides that every suit by a minor shall be instituted in his name by a person who shall be called the next friend of the minor. The Court may appoint a guardian ad litem.

queries.query: What is the provision for temporary injunction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 94 read with Order XXXIX provides that the Court may grant temporary injunction to restrain the defendant from committing any act or to prevent injury to the plaintiff.

queries.query: What is the provision for receiver?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 94 read with Order XL provides that the Court may appoint a receiver of any property before or after decree, and may remove any person from possession and commit the same to the receiver.

queries.query: What is the provision regarding costs in civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 35 provides that costs shall follow the event unless the Court orders otherwise for special reasons to be recorded. The Court has full power to determine by whom costs shall be paid.

queries.query: What is the provision for transfer of suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 22 deals with transfer between courts where suit may be instituted in more than one court. Section 24 gives general power of transfer. Section 25 gives Supreme Court power to transfer.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting temporary injunction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Under Order XXXIX, conditions include: prima facie case, balance of convenience in favor of applicant, irreparable injury if injunction not granted, and applicant must come with clean hands.

queries.query: What are the grounds for review of judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XLVII Rule 1 provides grounds: discovery of new and important matter or evidence, mistake or error apparent on face of record, or any other sufficient reason analogous to the above.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for res judicata to apply?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 11 requires: matter directly and substantially in issue, former suit between same parties, parties litigating under same title, court in former suit competent to try subsequent suit, and matter heard and finally decided.

queries.query: What are the requirements for a valid plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VII requires: name of court, name and address of parties, facts constituting cause of action, when it arose, facts showing court has jurisdiction, relief claimed, and plaint to be verified.

queries.query: What are the grounds for rejection of plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VII Rule 11 provides grounds: no cause of action disclosed, relief claimed undervalued and not corrected, insufficient stamp and not corrected, suit barred by any law, plaint not filed in duplicate, plaintiff fails to comply with court order.

queries.query: What are the conditions for second appeal to High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 100 requires: substantial question of law must be involved, no second appeal lies in cases where amount or value does not exceed threshold fixed by State Government, appeal must be from a decree passed in appeal.

queries.query: What are the limitations on revisional jurisdiction under Section 115?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 115 requires: case decided by subordinate court, jurisdiction exercised illegally or with material irregularity, or jurisdiction not exercised which it was duty to exercise. No revision lies against interlocutory orders.

queries.query: What are the rules for service of summons on defendant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order V provides: summons to be served personally, if not found then on adult family member, by affixture on outer door if refused, by registered post, substituted service if above modes fail, service by publication as last resort.

queries.query: What are the powers of Court in execution proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 51 provides powers: delivery of property, attachment and sale of property, arrest and detention, appointment of receiver. Section 47 allows determination of all questions including execution, discharge, or satisfaction.

queries.query: What are the conditions for appointment of receiver?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XL provides conditions: property is in danger of misappropriation or deterioration, preservation required pending suit, just and convenient for appointment, and receiver can be appointed before or after decree.

queries.query: What are the requirements for filing a written statement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VIII requires: written statement to be filed within 30 days (extendable to 90 days), specific denial of each allegation of fact, new facts constituting defence to be stated, must be verified.

queries.query: What are the grounds for setting aside ex parte decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order IX Rule 13 provides grounds: summons not duly served, defendant prevented by sufficient cause from appearing, and application must be filed within 30 days of knowledge of decree.

queries.query: What are the provisions regarding discovery and inspection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 30 and Order XI provide: court may order discovery of documents, interrogatories to be answered, inspection of documents and property, and admission of facts and documents.

queries.query: What are the conditions for attachment before judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXXVIII requires: defendant about to dispose of property with intent to obstruct decree, defendant about to remove property from jurisdiction, defendant acting to defraud creditors, and security may be required.

queries.query: What are the rules for examination of witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XVIII provides: plaintiff to begin, examination-in-chief, cross-examination, re-examination, court may put questions at any time, leading questions in cross-examination, and hostile witness may be cross-examined.

queries.query: What are the provisions for compromise of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXIII Rule 3 provides: suit may be adjusted wholly or in part by lawful agreement or compromise, court to record satisfaction, decree to be passed accordingly, and compromise can be set aside for fraud.

queries.query: What are the conditions for grant of mesne profits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2(12) and Order XX provide: profits actually received or could have been received with ordinary diligence, includes interest, court may make inquiry, and separate suit may be filed if amount not determined.

queries.query: What are the provisions for withdrawal of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXIII Rule 1 provides: plaintiff may abandon suit or part with leave of court, fresh suit barred unless court grants liberty to file fresh suit, and abandonment must be unconditional for liberty.

queries.query: What are the conditions for arrest of judgment debtor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXI provides: court to be satisfied of ability to pay, debtor given opportunity to show cause, detention in civil prison for period depending on decree amount, and women cannot be arrested for money decree.

queries.query: What are the rules for framing of issues?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XIV provides: issues arise when material proposition of fact or law is affirmed by one party and denied by another, court to frame issues from pleadings and examination, and may amend or strike out issues.

queries.query: What are the provisions for abatement of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXII provides: suit abates on death of sole plaintiff or defendant if right to sue does not survive, legal representative to be brought on record within limitation, and court may set aside abatement.

queries.query: What are the conditions for grant of specific performance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Specific Relief Act applies. Conditions include: valid contract exists, plaintiff ready and willing to perform, damages not adequate remedy, and contract must be specifically enforceable.

queries.query: What are the provisions for amendment of pleadings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VI Rule 17 provides: court may allow amendment at any stage on such terms as may be just, amendment cannot introduce new cause of action after limitation, and no amendment to be allowed if not necessary for determination.

queries.query: What are the rules for execution of decree for possession?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXI provides: decree for delivery of possession to be executed by removing persons bound by decree, property to be delivered to decree-holder, and resistance may be removed by force if necessary.

queries.query: What are the conditions for granting adjournment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 35B and Order XVII provide: court may grant adjournment for sufficient cause, costs may be imposed for adjournment, maximum three adjournments per party, and witness expenses may be awarded.

queries.query: What are the provisions for restitution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 144 provides: if decree is varied or reversed in appeal, court shall order restitution of what was received under decree, and party entitled to restitution may apply to court which passed decree.

queries.query: What are the rules for filing counter-claim?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VIII Rule 6A provides: defendant may set up counter-claim against plaintiff's claim, counter-claim to have same effect as cross-suit, and court may try claim and counter-claim together or separately.

queries.query: What are the provisions for summary judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XIII-A provides: commercial courts may grant summary judgment where defendant has no real prospect of defending, plaintiff must show cause of action, and defendant has no triable issue.

queries.query: What are the conditions for grant of perpetual injunction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Specific Relief Act applies. Conditions include: invasion of right proved or admitted, damages not adequate, defendant bound by contract or obligation, and injunction necessary to prevent breach.

queries.query: What are the provisions for caveat?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 148A provides: any person claiming right to appear may lodge caveat, caveat valid for 90 days, court to serve notice on caveator before granting ex parte relief, and caveator to serve copy on person expected to apply.

queries.query: What are the requirements for suit to be representative suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order I Rule 8 provides: numerous persons having same interest, one or more may sue with court's permission, notice to all interested persons, and decree binding on all represented.

queries.query: What are the grounds for dismissal of suit for default?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order IX provides: plaintiff absent when suit called on for hearing, plaintiff fails to take required step, and court may restore suit if sufficient cause shown for absence.

queries.query: What are the provisions for set-off in civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order VIII Rule 6 provides: defendant may claim set-off for ascertained sum legally recoverable, set-off must be within pecuniary jurisdiction, and same effect as plaint in cross-suit.

queries.query: How does res judicata under Section 11 relate to the doctrine of stay of suit under Section 10?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 10 prevents trial when matter is pending in prior suit (stay of proceedings). Section 11 bars a subsequent suit when matter was finally decided in prior suit. Section 10 applies during pendency while Section 11 applies after decision.

queries.query: What is the relationship between first appeal under Section 96 and second appeal under Section 100?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 provides for first appeal from original decree on facts and law. Section 100 provides second appeal to High Court only on substantial question of law. Second appeal is restricted, unlike first appeal which is on merits.

queries.query: How does revision under Section 115 differ from review under Section 114?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 114 review is by same court which passed decree for discovery of new evidence or error apparent on face of record. Section 115 revision is by High Court for jurisdictional errors. Review lies against final orders, revision against any case decided.

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 47 and Section 60 in execution proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 47 empowers court executing decree to determine all questions including what property is liable to attachment. Section 60 specifies which properties can be attached. Court under Section 47 applies Section 60 to determine attachable property.

queries.query: How does Section 35 on costs interact with Section 35A on compensatory costs?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 35 provides general rule that costs follow the event. Section 35A provides additional compensatory costs for false or vexatious claims or defences. Both can be awarded together but Section 35A requires finding of false or vexatious conduct.

queries.query: What is the relationship between inherent powers under Section 151 and revision under Section 115?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 151 preserves inherent powers for ends of justice. Section 115 gives supervisory jurisdiction to High Court. Section 151 cannot be used to override Section 115 limitations, but may supplement where Section 115 does not apply.

queries.query: How does Section 9 jurisdiction relate to Section 11 res judicata bar?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 9 gives courts jurisdiction over all civil suits unless barred. Section 11 creates a bar by making prior decision conclusive. If Section 11 applies, the court under Section 9 cannot try the subsequent suit - it's impliedly barred.

queries.query: What is the connection between Sections 79 and 80 regarding suits against Government?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 79 prescribes the proper party name for suits involving Government (Union of India/State). Section 80 requires mandatory two-month notice before instituting suit. Both must be complied with - proper party under Section 79 and notice under Section 80.

queries.query: How does Section 89 on ADR relate to Section 151 inherent powers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 89 provides specific mechanism for referring disputes to ADR. Section 151 preserves general inherent powers. Court can use Section 151 to promote settlement even without formal Section 89 reference, but Section 89 provides structured framework.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Section 94 supplemental proceedings and Order XXXIX injunctions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 94 provides the substantive power for supplemental proceedings including injunctions. Order XXXIX provides the procedural framework for granting temporary injunctions. Section 94 is the source of power, Order XXXIX is the procedure.

queries.query: How does Section 16 on jurisdiction for immovable property interact with Section 20 for other suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 16 mandates suit for immovable property be filed where property is situated. Section 20 applies to other suits where defendant resides or cause of action arises. Section 16 is mandatory and overrides Section 20 for immovable property.

queries.query: What is the connection between execution under Section 51 and attachment under Section 60?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 51 lists modes of execution including attachment and sale. Section 60 specifies which properties are liable to attachment. Court must first identify attachable property under Section 60 before proceeding with execution under Section 51.

queries.query: How does Section 13 on foreign judgments relate to Section 44A on reciprocating territory?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 13 lists when foreign judgment is not conclusive. Section 44A provides simplified execution of decrees from reciprocating territories. Section 44A decrees are directly executable but still subject to Section 13 exceptions.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Section 107 appellate powers and Section 96 appeal provisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 creates the right of appeal from original decree. Section 107 defines the powers of the appellate court. Section 96 gives jurisdiction to hear appeal, Section 107 specifies what appellate court can do with that jurisdiction.

queries.query: How does Section 22 transfer of suits relate to Section 25 Supreme Court transfer power?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 22 deals with transfer when suit can be filed in multiple courts. Section 24 gives general transfer power to District/High Court. Section 25 gives Supreme Court power to transfer between states. Hierarchy: Section 22 (limited) → Section 24 (general) → Section 25 (national).

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 38 and Section 39 on execution of decrees?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 38 specifies which court can execute a decree (court which passed it or court to which it's transferred). Section 39 provides procedure for transfer of decree for execution. Section 38 defines competent court, Section 39 enables transfer to that court.

queries.query: How does Section 144 restitution relate to appellate powers under Section 107?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 107 empowers appellate court to vary or reverse decree. Section 144 provides for restitution when decree is varied or reversed. Section 144 is consequential to Section 107 - once appellate court modifies decree, restitution follows.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Order XXXVIII attachment before judgment and Section 60?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXXVIII (under Section 94) allows attachment before judgment to secure decree. Section 60 specifies attachable properties. Attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII must comply with Section 60 exemptions.

queries.query: How does Section 2 definition of decree relate to Section 96 appeal provisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2(2) defines decree as formal expression of adjudication. Section 96 provides appeal from original decree. Only decisions qualifying as 'decree' under Section 2(2) are appealable under Section 96. Orders are dealt with under Section 104.

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 91 public nuisance suits and Section 92 public charities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 91 provides for suits regarding public nuisances and wrongful acts affecting public. Section 92 provides for suits concerning public charitable or religious trusts. Both require leave of court or Advocate-General involvement, protecting public interest.

queries.query: How does Section 47 determination of questions relate to Section 37 definition of court which passed decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 37 defines which court is deemed to have passed the decree for execution purposes. Section 47 empowers that court to determine all questions arising in execution. Section 37 identifies the competent court, Section 47 defines its powers.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Section 55 arrest in execution and Section 56 protection of women?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 55 provides for arrest and detention of judgment debtor in execution. Section 56 creates an exception prohibiting arrest or detention of women in execution of money decree. Section 56 is a specific exception to Section 55 based on gender.

queries.query: How does Order XXIII withdrawal of suit relate to Order I addition of parties?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXIII Rule 1 permits withdrawal of suit. Order I allows addition and substitution of parties. If party is added under Order I, withdrawal of suit affects all parties. Order XXIII withdrawal must consider all parties under Order I.

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 27 summons and Order V service of summons?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 27 requires court to issue summons to defendant on suit being instituted. Order V provides detailed procedure for service of summons including modes of service, substituted service, and deemed service. Section 27 mandates summons, Order V provides mechanics.

queries.query: How does Section 97 appeal from final decree relate to Section 96 first appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 provides general right of first appeal from original decree. Section 97 bars appeal from final decree where no appeal was filed against preliminary decree. This prevents parties from raising preliminary decree issues at final decree stage.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Section 73 rateable distribution and Section 64 effect of attachment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 64 makes private transfers void after attachment. Section 73 provides rateable distribution among decree-holders. Attached property under Section 64 is preserved for distribution under Section 73 among applying decree-holders.

queries.query: How does Section 49 transferee's liability relate to Section 64 void alienation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 49 makes decree executable against transferee of property. Section 64 voids alienations after attachment. Section 49 applies to transfers before attachment, Section 64 applies after attachment. Both protect decree-holder but at different stages.

queries.query: What is the connection between Order IX dismissal for default and Section 96 appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order IX provides for dismissal when plaintiff defaults. Section 96 provides appeal from original decree. An order of dismissal under Order IX Rule 8 is a decree appealable under Section 96. Party can either appeal under Section 96 or seek restoration under Order IX.

queries.query: How does Section 3 subordination of courts relate to Section 115 revisional jurisdiction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 3 establishes the hierarchy and subordination of civil courts. Section 115 gives High Court supervisory jurisdiction over subordinate courts. The subordination under Section 3 enables the supervisory power under Section 115.

queries.query: What is the relationship between Order XX judgment and Section 33 judgment and decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 33 requires pronouncement of judgment and signing of decree. Order XX provides detailed rules for contents of judgment and decree. Section 33 mandates the requirement, Order XX provides the procedure and format.

queries.query: How does Order XXII abatement interact with Section 50 legal representative?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order XXII deals with abatement on death of party and bringing legal representatives on record. Section 50 allows execution against legal representative. Order XXII determines who the legal representative is, Section 50 allows execution against them.

queries.query: What is the connection between Section 6 pecuniary jurisdiction and Section 15 place of suing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 6 establishes pecuniary jurisdiction based on value of subject matter. Section 15 determines the local court where suit must be filed. Both must be satisfied - court must have both pecuniary jurisdiction under Section 6 and territorial jurisdiction under Section 15.

queries.query: How does Section 104 appeal from orders relate to Section 105 other orders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 104 lists specific orders from which appeal lies. Section 105 states that orders not mentioned in Section 104 shall not be appealable but may be challenged in appeal from decree. Section 104 creates appealable category, Section 105 preserves other challenges.

queries.query: What is the doctrine of res judicata?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A matter directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties in a Court competent to try it, decided on merits, cannot be re-agitated.

queries.query: What is res sub judice under the Code of Civil Procedure?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit pending in another Court of concurrent jurisdiction.

queries.query: When can a foreign judgment be ignored by Indian courts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A foreign judgment is not conclusive if pronounced by a court without jurisdiction, without giving fair opportunity to defendant, obtained by fraud, or contrary to Indian law.

queries.query: What is the general rule about place of suing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Subject to the pecuniary and other limitations, a suit may be instituted in a Court within whose local jurisdiction the defendant resides or carries on business or the cause of action arose.

queries.query: What notice must be given before suing the government?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No suit shall be instituted against the Government or a public officer in respect of any act done in official capacity until the expiry of two months after a notice has been delivered.

queries.query: What is a first appeal under the CPC?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An appeal shall lie from every decree passed by any Court exercising original jurisdiction to the Court authorized to hear appeals from those decisions.

queries.query: When does a second appeal lie?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A second appeal shall lie to the High Court only on a substantial question of law.

queries.query: What is the power of review?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any person considering himself aggrieved by a decree or order may apply for review to the Court which passed the decree or order.

queries.query: What is the revisional power of High Court under Section 115?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court may call for the record of any case decided by any Court subordinate to it in which no appeal lies and in which the subordinate Court appears to have acted with material irregularity.

queries.query: What are inherent powers of court under Section 151?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Nothing in the Code shall be deemed to limit or affect the inherent power of the Court to make orders necessary to do justice or to prevent abuse of the process.

queries.query: What is the law relating to institution of suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every suit shall be instituted by the presentation of a plaint or in such other manner as may be prescribed.

queries.query: What property is exempt from attachment in execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Property of certain classes is not liable to attachment including necessaries of life, tools of artisans, agricultural implements, and salaries to a specified extent.

queries.query: What is a temporary injunction under Order 39?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A temporary injunction may be granted to restrain the defendant from committing the act complained of if the matter is urgent and there is a probability of success on merits.

queries.query: What is the purpose of a receiver under Order 40?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A receiver may be appointed to take custody of any property which is the subject matter of a suit for its preservation pending the suit.

queries.query: What are the grounds for rejection of plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The plaint shall be rejected where it does not disclose a cause of action, where the relief claimed is undervalued, where it is barred by any law, or where it is insufficiently stamped.

queries.query: What is a written statement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The defendant shall present a written statement of his defence within 30 days of service of summons, specifically denying each allegation not admitted and setting out any counter-claim.

queries.query: What is the rule regarding set-off?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A defendant in a suit for recovery of money may claim a set-off against the plaintiff's demand for any ascertained sum of money legally recoverable from the plaintiff.

queries.query: What are the conditions for grant of temporary injunction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must be satisfied that there is a prima facie case, balance of convenience favours the applicant, and irreparable harm would result if injunction is refused.

queries.query: What is the procedure for amendment of pleadings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings at any stage of the proceedings in such manner as may be just on such terms as to costs as may be just.

queries.query: What is the meaning of a decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Decree means the formal expression of an adjudication which conclusively determines the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit.

queries.query: What is the doctrine of constructive res judicata?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Explanation IV to Section 11 provides that any matter which might and ought to have been made a ground of defence in the former suit shall be deemed to have been a matter directly and substantially in issue.

queries.query: What is the procedure for service of summons by substituted service?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the Court is satisfied that there is reason to believe the defendant is evading service, it may order service by affixing a copy at the place of residence or by advertisement.

queries.query: What are the rules regarding discovery by interrogatories?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any party may apply for an order to administer interrogatories to the other party relating to any matter in question in the suit for the purpose of disposing of the cause.

queries.query: What is the power to settle issues?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Issues arise when a material proposition of fact or law is affirmed by one party and denied by the other; the Court frames issues at the first hearing of the suit.

queries.query: What is the rule on judgment on admissions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any party may at any stage apply for judgment based on admissions of fact made by the other party in the pleadings, oral examination or otherwise.

queries.query: What is the rule regarding joinder of parties?
queries.ground_truth_answer: All persons may be joined as plaintiffs in whom any right to relief in respect of the same act, transaction, or series of transactions arises.

queries.query: What are the rules governing pleadings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every pleading shall contain a statement of material facts on which the party pleading relies for his claim or defence but not the evidence by which they are to be proved.

queries.query: What is a summary suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Summary suits may be filed for recovery of money on bills of exchange, hundis, promissory notes or on a written contract for a liquidated sum of money.

queries.query: What is the procedure for withdrawal of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A plaintiff may at any time abandon his suit or abandon part of his claim; where a suit is withdrawn the defendant is entitled to his costs.

queries.query: What is the procedure for compromise of suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where it is proved to the Court that a suit has been adjusted by any lawful agreement or compromise the Court shall pass a decree in accordance with such agreement.

queries.query: What is execution of decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Application for execution of a decree must be made to the Court which passed the decree; several modes of execution are available including delivery of property and attachment and sale.

queries.query: What is the power of appellate court in first appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Appellate Court has the same powers and shall perform the same duties as are conferred and imposed by the Code on Courts of original jurisdiction.

queries.query: What is a decree for specific performance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A decree for specific performance of a contract or for an injunction shall be enforced by attachment and sale of property of the party required to perform or obey.

queries.query: What is the procedure for examination of judgment debtor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a decree is for money and has not been fully satisfied, the decree holder may apply to the Court for examination of the judgment debtor as to his property.

queries.query: What are the provisions for appeals from orders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An appeal shall lie from every order specified in Section 104 including orders refusing leave to sue as a pauper, granting or refusing injunctions, and appointing or refusing to appoint a receiver.

queries.query: What is the rule on production of additional evidence in appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The parties are not entitled to produce additional evidence in appeal; the Appellate Court may however allow it if it was not within the knowledge of the party or could not be produced at trial.

queries.query: What is the doctrine of election of remedies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A plaintiff suing for a portion of a claim may not afterwards sue for the portion omitted; the whole claim must be included in one suit.

queries.query: What is the rule regarding suits by paupers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any person entitled to sue but unable to pay court fees may apply to the Court to be permitted to sue as an indigent person; the Court must inquire into means.

queries.query: What is the power of Court to pass judgment for defendant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a case has been adjourned for delivery of judgment and the party whose turn it was to produce evidence has not done so, the Court may pronounce judgment.

queries.query: What is a cross-objection in appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any respondent in appeal may, not later than one month after service of notice of day of hearing, present a memorandum of objections and such cross-objections shall be heard with the appeal.

queries.query: What is the limitation for execution of decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An application for execution of decree must be made within twelve years from the date of the decree or order.

queries.query: What is attachment before judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order attachment of property before judgment where the defendant is about to dispose of the whole or any part of his property with intent to obstruct execution.

queries.query: What is the rule for misjoinder of causes of action?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The plaintiff may unite in the same suit several causes of action against the same defendant; where parties are the same the Court has discretion to try causes together.

queries.query: What are the provisions for suits against public charities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A suit claiming relief of a public nature in respect of trusts for charitable or religious purposes may be brought by the Advocate General or two or more persons with leave of the Court.

queries.query: What is the rule on costs?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Costs shall follow the event; the Court has discretion to direct by whom and to what extent costs shall be paid; costs must be commensurate with the conduct of the parties.

queries.query: What is the law on interest in civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may award interest on the principal sum adjudged from the date of suit to the date of the decree and also interest on the aggregate from decree to payment.

queries.query: What is the meaning of judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Judgment means the statement given by the Judge of the grounds of a decree or order; it must contain a concise statement of the case, points for determination, decision thereon, and reasons.

queries.query: What is the procedure for taking accounts in civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where the Court has ordered accounts to be taken, the accounts shall be settled by the Court which may appoint an officer to take the accounts.

queries.query: What is a preliminary decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A preliminary decree is one which determines certain rights and liabilities but does not finally dispose of the suit; a final decree follows after accounts or partition.

queries.query: What are the provisions for suits by or against partnerships?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any two or more persons claiming or being liable as partners may sue or be sued in the name of the firm, and the partners need not be individually named in the pleadings.

queries.query: What is the power of court regarding supplemental proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may grant a temporary injunction, make interlocutory orders, appoint a receiver, and in the interests of justice order other supplemental proceedings.

queries.query: What is the law on objections to jurisdiction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No objection as to the place of suing shall be allowed by any Appellate or Revisional Court unless such objection was taken in the Court of first instance and there has been a consequent failure of justice.

queries.query: What is the power of Court for general transfer of suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court or District Court may transfer any suit from one Court to another on application or on its own motion, where expedient for ends of justice.

queries.query: What is the rule on abatement of appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Every appeal shall abate on the death of the sole appellant unless a legal representative of the deceased is brought on record within the prescribed time.

queries.query: What is the procedure for execution against legal representatives?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a judgment debtor dies after passing of decree the decree may be executed against the legal representatives.

queries.query: What is the effect of non-filing of written statement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the defendant fails to present a written statement within the time permitted the Court may pronounce judgment on the basis of the plaint or hold an ex parte hearing.

queries.query: What are the provisions for vexatious litigation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a claim or defence is found to be false or vexatious the Court may award compensatory costs not exceeding three thousand rupees to the other party.

queries.query: What is the rule on addition or substitution of parties?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No suit shall be defeated by reason of misjoinder or non-joinder of parties; the Court may deal with the matter in controversy in the suit as it relates to the parties before it.

queries.query: What is the procedure for execution by attachment of property?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a decree directs the defendant to pay money and it is not paid, the decree holder may apply for attachment of property of the judgment debtor.

queries.query: What is the order of preference in distribution of proceeds of sale?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where property is sold in execution, the proceeds shall be distributed rateably among all decree holders holding decrees against the same judgment debtor.

queries.query: What is the procedure for arrest and detention in execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A judgment debtor may be arrested by warrant; civil imprisonment can be directed for a maximum period of three months; certain categories are exempt from arrest.

queries.query: What are the rules for filing a plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The plaint shall contain the name of the court, name and description of the plaintiff and defendant, the facts constituting the cause of action, the relief claimed and a statement of value of the subject matter.

queries.query: What are the special provisions for suits against foreign States?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A foreign State may sue in any competent Court; but suits against a foreign State require consent of the Central Government and service on the Head of Mission or Secretary of the foreign State.

queries.query: What is the procedure for reference to High Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any Court may, before passing a decree, state a case and refer it for the opinion of the High Court if it doubts the correctness of a High Court decree on a point of law.

queries.query: What is the effect of death of a party to the suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If a party to the suit dies and the right to sue survives, the suit shall not abate but shall continue by or against his legal representative.

queries.query: What is the rule on joinder of defendants?
queries.ground_truth_answer: All persons may be joined as defendants against whom any right to relief in respect of the same act or transaction is alleged to exist whether jointly, severally, or in the alternative.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for the plea of res judicata to succeed?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The matter must be directly and substantially in issue in both suits, the former suit must have been between the same parties or persons claiming under them, and the Court must have been competent to try it and the decision must be on merits.

queries.query: What conditions must be met to stay a suit under Section 10?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The matter in issue must be substantially the same in both suits, both suits must be between the same parties, the former suit must have been previously instituted, and the Court trying the former suit must be competent.

queries.query: When can the Court reject a plaint under Order 7 Rule 11?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The plaint must be rejected when it discloses no cause of action, when relief is undervalued and plaintiff fails to correct on being required, when it is barred by law, or when it is insufficiently stamped.

queries.query: What conditions apply to grant of temporary injunction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Three conditions must be met: prima facie case, balance of convenience in favour of the applicant, and irreparable injury if injunction is refused; the Court also considers conduct of parties.

queries.query: What conditions must exist for a second appeal to lie?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A second appeal lies only on a substantial question of law; the High Court must formulate the question; findings of fact by lower courts are binding; the question must arise from the decree itself.

queries.query: Under what conditions can the Court exercise inherent powers under Section 151?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may exercise inherent powers to make orders necessary for doing justice, to prevent abuse of process; these powers cannot be used to circumvent express provisions of the Code.

queries.query: What conditions apply for setting aside ex parte decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The defendant must show sufficient cause for non-appearance; the application must be filed within 30 days of knowledge of the decree; there must be a meritorious defence disclosed.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for amendment of pleadings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Amendment must be necessary for determining the real question in controversy; it must not cause injustice to the other side that cannot be compensated in costs; after commencement of trial stricter standard applies.

queries.query: What conditions apply to review of judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Review lies only on discovery of new and important matter which could not be found earlier, or mistake apparent on the face of the record, or for other sufficient reasons; review cannot be used as a second appeal.

queries.query: Under what conditions may additional evidence be admitted in appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Additional evidence may only be allowed if the party could not have produced it at the trial with reasonable diligence, or if it is required for the decision of the Court, or if the Court requires it to enable it to pronounce judgment.

queries.query: What conditions justify exercise of revisional jurisdiction under Section 115?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The subordinate Court must have acted without jurisdiction or in excess of jurisdiction, or failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or acted with material irregularity or illegality; revision cannot be used to correct errors of fact.

queries.query: What conditions apply to granting summary judgment under Order 12 Rule 6?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Judgment on admissions can be given when a party has made clear, unambiguous admissions in pleadings; the Court has discretion to give judgment immediately without waiting for trial.

queries.query: What conditions justify appointment of a receiver?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must be satisfied that it is just and convenient to appoint a receiver; there must be danger that the property will be removed, damaged, or its value diminished; the party must have a prima facie right.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before filing a suit against the Government?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A notice of two months must be given stating the cause of action, the name and place of abode of the plaintiff, and the relief claimed; the notice must be delivered to the Secretary or Collector.

queries.query: Under what conditions can a suit be compromised?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The compromise must be lawful; it must be in writing and signed; the Court must record it; a party minor or incapacitated requires guardian's consent and Court approval.

queries.query: What conditions justify withdrawal of suit with liberty to file fresh suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must be satisfied that there is sufficient cause for withdrawal; liberty to file fresh suit is granted only when withdrawal is for formal defect or there is sufficient ground; otherwise withdrawal bars a fresh suit.

queries.query: What conditions apply to execution of a money decree by arrest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Civil imprisonment can be ordered only when the Court is satisfied the judgment debtor has means to pay but refuses; certain persons are exempt including women, judicial officers, and government servants.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for attachment before judgment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must be satisfied that the defendant is about to dispose of or remove his property with intent to obstruct execution; there must be a prima facie case on merits.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the rule in Order 2 Rule 2 regarding splitting of claims?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A plaintiff must include the whole claim in one suit; if he omits any part of the claim he shall not afterwards sue for the part omitted; the bar applies to claims arising from the same cause of action.

queries.query: What are the conditions for setting aside a sale in execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An application to set aside sale must be filed within 60 days of sale; the applicant must pay the purchase money to the Court; there must be material irregularity causing substantial injury.

queries.query: What conditions apply before a Court can exercise jurisdiction under Section 9?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court must have territorial, pecuniary, and subject matter jurisdiction; if any court is to be excluded from jurisdiction there must be express or implied exclusion by a statute.

queries.query: What conditions apply for dismissal for default of appearance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If summons was duly served and the plaintiff fails to appear on the day fixed the Court may dismiss the suit; the plaintiff may apply to restore within 30 days showing sufficient cause.

queries.query: What conditions justify striking out pleadings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may strike out any matter in any pleading which is scandalous, frivolous, vexatious, or tends to prejudice, embarrass, or delay the fair trial.

queries.query: What conditions apply for an appeal against interlocutory order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An appeal lies only from orders specified in Order 43; other interlocutory orders can be challenged only at the time of appeal from the final decree; no separate appeal lies unless expressly provided.

queries.query: What conditions apply for establishing constructive res judicata?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The matter must be one which ought to have been raised in the previous suit; the party must have had an opportunity to raise it; if the plea could have been raised and was not, it is barred.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for return of plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The plaint shall be returned for presentation to the proper Court if it is presented to a Court which lacks territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction; the Court must specify to which court it should be presented.

queries.query: What conditions justify interference with findings of fact in second appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The High Court in second appeal can interfere with findings of fact only when they are based on misreading or ignoring evidence, or when the findings are perverse; pure questions of fact cannot be re-examined.

queries.query: What conditions apply for grant of leave to defend in summary suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Leave to defend shall be granted unconditionally if the defendant shows a triable issue; conditional leave may be given if there is a defence but it is shadowy; if defence is frivolous leave shall be refused.

queries.query: What conditions apply for execution of decree for specific performance?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A decree for specific performance shall be enforced by attachment of property; if the defendant fails to perform within the time ordered the Court may direct performance by another person.

queries.query: What conditions justify the Court ordering accounts in a partnership suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An account may be ordered when partnership assets are being claimed; a preliminary decree is passed directing accounts; a final decree is passed after settlement of accounts.

queries.query: What conditions apply for filing a cross-objection in appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Cross-objections must be filed within one month of notice of hearing; they must relate to a matter decided against the respondent; they are heard with the main appeal and abate with it.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the Court ordering discovery and inspection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order production of documents for inspection if they relate to matters in question in the suit; party possessing them must be a party to the suit; privilege attaches to certain documents.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the objection that a suit is barred by limitation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A plaint may be rejected if the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law including the Limitation Act; the bar must be apparent on the face of the plaint.

queries.query: What conditions justify the Court granting costs on solicitor-client basis?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Such costs are awarded when one party has acted dishonestly, has put the other to unnecessary expense, or has caused the litigation by unreasonable conduct; it is an exception to the general rule.

queries.query: What conditions apply to execution of a decree passed ex parte?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An ex parte decree may be set aside on application; if it is not set aside it remains a valid decree; an ex parte decree may be executed in the normal manner.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for the Court to pronounce judgment on issues?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Issues shall be determined before evidence is recorded; at the conclusion of the suit the Court must pronounce judgment on all issues; the Court may dispose of the suit on a preliminary issue.

queries.query: What conditions justify allowing a plea of set-off?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A set-off is permissible when it is for an ascertained sum of money legally recoverable from the plaintiff; it cannot exceed the plaintiff's claim; it reduces the amount recoverable by the plaintiff.

queries.query: What conditions apply to consolidation of suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may order consolidation of two or more suits if the suits involve common questions of law or fact, or arise out of the same transaction; consolidation promotes economy and consistency.

queries.query: What conditions justify substituted service under Order 5 Rule 20?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Substituted service may be ordered when the defendant is deliberately evading service; the Court must be satisfied that ordinary modes of service have failed; the order must state the mode of substituted service.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the rule that costs must follow the event?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Costs normally follow the event; but the Court may depart from this rule when a successful party has raised frivolous issues, has been guilty of misconduct, or when the suit is partly decreed.

queries.query: What conditions apply for directing that accounts be taken before decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In suits for dissolution of partnership, administration of estate, or redemption of mortgage, the Court passes a preliminary decree and directs accounts before passing a final decree.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power to add new parties to the suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A person necessary for a complete adjudication of the controversy may be added as a party; if a necessary party is not joined the suit may be dismissed; a proper party may be added at the Court's discretion.

queries.query: What conditions apply for the Court to take up an issue as a preliminary issue?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An issue of law or a mixed issue of law and fact may be tried as a preliminary issue; if the preliminary issue disposes of the suit no further trial is needed; the Court has discretion.

queries.query: What conditions justify making an interlocutory order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An interlocutory order may be made to preserve the subject matter, to prevent irreparable injury, or to balance the competing claims of the parties pending the final decision.

queries.query: What conditions apply to revival of a suit after abatement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An application to set aside abatement must be filed within 90 days of the death; sufficient cause must be shown; if a suit abates the decree passed in it is a nullity.

queries.query: What conditions apply for receiving documentary evidence in civil suits?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Documents to be used by parties must be produced with the plaint or written statement; documents not produced may be admitted on application; secondary evidence may be admitted if primary is unavailable.

queries.query: What conditions apply to decreeing a suit on the basis of admissions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Judgment on admissions can be given at any stage; the admission must be clear and unambiguous; the Court retains discretion not to give judgment even if there are admissions; relief given must follow from the admission.

queries.query: What conditions apply for a cross-suit to be tried with the main suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A cross-suit involves the same parties and same subject matter; the Court may order both to be tried together; if tried separately res judicata or estoppel may apply.

queries.query: What conditions must be met before a Court can grant relief not prayed for?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court cannot grant relief not prayed for except where the plaintiff has included a prayer for general or other relief; the Court may mould the relief to fit the proved facts.

queries.query: What conditions apply for summary determination of questions without full trial?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A Court of equity can try and decide a suit summarily when both parties agree or when the questions are simple; summary determination must not prejudice the rights of the parties.

queries.query: What conditions justify granting an injunction to restrain proceedings in another Court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An anti-suit injunction may be granted when there is harassment by multiple proceedings, when Indian courts have a stronger connection to the dispute, and when it is necessary to prevent injustice.

queries.query: What conditions apply to adjournments under Order 17 Rule 1?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Adjournments should not be granted as a matter of course; the party must show sufficient cause; no adjournment shall be granted more than three times during a hearing except for exceptional circumstances.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for the Court to allow interrogatories?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Interrogatories must relate to any matter in question in the suit; they must not be scandalous or oppressive; the Court may disallow interrogatories which are not necessary for fairly disposing of the suit.

queries.query: What conditions apply to ordering security for costs?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the plaintiff is residing out of India or is a person of no means the Court may order him to furnish security for costs; failure to furnish may result in dismissal.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for the Court to accept secondary evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Secondary evidence is admissible when original is lost or destroyed, when the party producing it is not able to obtain possession of the original in reasonable time, or when it is a public document.

queries.query: What conditions apply to ex parte hearing and decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: When the defendant fails to appear on the day fixed for hearing and summons was duly served, the Court may hear the suit ex parte; the plaintiff must still prove his case.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power of Court to call witnesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Court may at any time before judgment require the attendance of any person for examination; the Court may also recall and re-examine a witness already examined.

queries.query: What conditions justify reopening the case after judgment is reserved?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Once a judgment is reserved it should be pronounced within 30 days; the case can be reopened only for exceptional reasons; parties cannot as of right demand reopening.

queries.query: What conditions apply for the Court to permit filing of additional written statement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Additional written statement is permissible only with leave of the Court; it must deal with new matters that arose after filing of written statement; it cannot introduce matters that could have been pleaded earlier.

queries.query: What conditions apply for objection to jurisdiction to be considered valid?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Objection must be taken at the earliest opportunity at the Court of first instance; if not taken there it cannot be raised later; failure of justice must also be shown.

queries.query: What conditions apply for treating a counter-claim as a separate suit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A counter-claim must be filed with or before filing written statement; it shall be treated as a plaint for a cross-suit; if the plaintiff fails, the counter-claim may still succeed.

queries.query: What conditions justify a decree nisi in matrimonial cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where a suit abates by reason of death of one of the parties, the Court may substitute the legal representative; in matrimonial proceedings the Court has special powers.

queries.query: What conditions apply to enforcement of decree of foreign court?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A foreign decree may be executed as if passed by an Indian court unless it falls within the exceptions; the decree must be final and conclusive; the foreign court must have had jurisdiction.

queries.query: What conditions must be satisfied for review to lie on discovery of new evidence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The evidence must be new and important; it must not have been within the knowledge of the applicant or could not be produced at the time of the original decree; it must be likely to affect the decision.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the doctrine of waiver in civil proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Waiver of an objection to jurisdiction must be voluntary and intentional; it must be clear that the party has acquiesced in the jurisdiction; a party cannot approbate and reprobate.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the distinction between decree and order?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A decree conclusively determines the rights of the parties; an order is every formal expression of decision which is not a decree; the distinction is important because appeals lie differently from decrees and orders.

queries.query: What conditions justify an appeal from an order refusing to set aside ex parte decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An appeal lies from an order refusing to set aside an ex parte decree; the applicant must show that the ex parte decree was passed in his absence without sufficient cause shown in his application.

queries.query: How do Sections 10 and 11 complement each other in protecting against multiplicity of proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 10 stays concurrent proceedings to prevent conflicting decisions; Section 11 bars re-litigation after a final decision; together they protect parties from being vexed twice for the same cause.

queries.query: How do Sections 96 and 100 define the appellate hierarchy in civil cases?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 provides for first appeal from original decree on questions of fact and law; Section 100 limits second appeal to questions of law only; together they create a two-tier appellate system with decreasing scope of review.

queries.query: How do Sections 114 and 115 differ in review and revision?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 114 enables a party to apply to the same Court that passed the decree for review on discovery of new facts or error on record; Section 115 enables the High Court to revise decisions of subordinate courts; review is by the same court and revision by a superior court.

queries.query: How do Sections 151 and 94 together define supplemental and inherent powers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 94 specifies supplemental proceedings including injunctions; Section 151 preserves inherent powers for matters not covered; when a specific provision exists the general inherent power should not be resorted to.

queries.query: How do Sections 9 and 20 together determine which court has jurisdiction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 9 provides for courts to try all civil suits unless barred; Section 20 specifies the place where suit may be instituted based on residence of defendant or place where cause of action arose; both must be satisfied for competent jurisdiction.

queries.query: How do Orders 39 and 40 provide different interim relief mechanisms?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 39 provides for temporary injunction to restrain a party from doing acts; Order 40 provides for appointment of receiver to manage disputed property; both are interim measures but one restrains a party and the other appoints a custodian.

queries.query: How do Sections 96 and 107 define the powers at different levels of appeal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 provides for first appeal; Section 107 gives the Appellate Court the same powers as a trial court including power to order production of evidence; the Appellate Court can rehear and reach different findings.

queries.query: How do Orders 7 Rule 11 and Order 14 Rule 2 interact in early disposal?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 7 Rule 11 enables rejection at the plaint stage; Order 14 Rule 2 enables disposal on preliminary issue without evidence; both enable early termination but at different stages of proceedings.

queries.query: How do Sections 35 and 35A differ regarding costs?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 35 provides for general costs following the event; Section 35A provides for compensatory costs in cases of false or vexatious claims; the former is a general provision and the latter a penalty.

queries.query: How do Orders 23 Rule 1 and 23 Rule 3 differ in withdrawal and compromise?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 23 Rule 1 enables a party to withdraw from the suit; Order 23 Rule 3 enables parties to settle by compromise which the Court records as a decree; in withdrawal there is no settlement but in compromise there is.

queries.query: How do Orders 38 Rule 1 and 39 Rule 1 provide different types of interim relief?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 38 Rule 1 protects the decree by attaching property before judgment is passed; Order 39 Rule 1 restrains the party from doing the act complained of; both are preventive but one protects assets and the other restrains conduct.

queries.query: How do Sections 11 and 13 relate to domestic and foreign judgments?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 11 deals with domestic res judicata; Section 13 deals with foreign judgments and specifies when they are not conclusive; a foreign judgment can operate as res judicata unless it falls within the exceptions in Section 13.

queries.query: How do Sections 96 and 100 together set the standard for interference on facts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In first appeal under Section 96 the court can reassess evidence and record different findings of fact; in second appeal under Section 100 findings of fact are final and only questions of law can be raised.

queries.query: How do Orders 6 Rule 17 and 7 Rule 10 relate to amendment and return of plaint?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 6 Rule 17 enables amendment to correct defects in the plaint; Order 7 Rule 10 enables return of plaint if there is a jurisdictional defect; amendment is used for substantive defects while return is for jurisdictional errors.

queries.query: How do Orders 41 Rule 27 and 9 Rule 13 deal with fresh evidence at different stages?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 41 Rule 27 restricts production of additional evidence in appeal to limited circumstances; Order 9 Rule 13 enables setting aside ex parte decree on sufficient cause including new evidence; both address circumstances where new evidence may change the outcome.

queries.query: How do Sections 34 and 35 together deal with costs and interest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 34 empowers the Court to award interest on the decretal amount from date of suit to date of decree; Section 35 deals with costs; both are directions that form part of the decree and are enforceable.

queries.query: How do Orders 21 and 38 relate to execution and pre-judgment protection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 38 protects the plaintiff's ability to execute by attaching property before judgment; Order 21 provides for execution after the decree is passed; both deal with property but at different stages.

queries.query: How do Orders 8 Rule 1 and 8 Rule 9 relate to the defence?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 8 Rule 1 requires filing of written statement within 30 days; Order 8 Rule 9 provides consequences for failure including ex parte hearing; together they define both the obligation and the sanction.

queries.query: How do Sections 80 and 82 differ in suits against Government and Government property?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 80 requires prior notice for suits against Government or public officers; Section 82 restricts arrest of Government servants for contempt; both provide special protection to Government in litigation.

queries.query: How do Orders 39 Rule 1 and 39 Rule 2 differ in injunctions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 39 Rule 1 provides for injunction to restrain repetition of threatened acts; Order 39 Rule 2 provides for injunction to restrain continuation of wrongful acts; one prevents future acts and the other stops ongoing ones.

queries.query: How do Sections 96 and 104 define appeals from decrees and orders?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 96 provides for appeal from every original decree; Section 104 specifies orders from which appeal lies; decrees and orders are fundamentally different and have different routes of appeal.

queries.query: How do Orders 11 Rule 1 and 11 Rule 12 relate to interrogatories and inspection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 11 Rule 1 enables discovery by interrogatories; Order 11 Rule 12 enables discovery and inspection of documents; both are discovery mechanisms designed to ensure parties know the evidence against them before trial.

queries.query: How do Sections 114 and 100 differ in when they can be invoked?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Review under Section 114 must be made to the same Court that passed the decree; second appeal under Section 100 is to the High Court; review is for error apparent on face of record and second appeal is for substantial question of law.

queries.query: How do Orders 40 and 21 relate to receiver and execution?
queries.ground_truth_answer: A receiver may be appointed to manage property pending litigation; after decree the property may be subject to execution; if a receiver is in possession execution cannot proceed without Court's permission.

queries.query: How do Sections 9 and 115 interact regarding jurisdiction and revision?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 9 grants jurisdiction to try all civil suits; Section 115 enables the High Court to correct jurisdictional errors; revision lies when the subordinate Court has acted without jurisdiction or in excess of jurisdiction.

queries.query: How do Orders 1 Rule 1 and 1 Rule 3 govern joinder of plaintiffs and defendants?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 1 Rule 1 enables joinder of plaintiffs who have a common right to relief from the same transaction; Order 1 Rule 3 enables joinder of defendants who are jointly liable in the same transaction; both promote economy of litigation.

queries.query: How do Orders 7 and 8 define the pleading stage in civil proceedings?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Order 7 prescribes what must be in the plaint including the cause of action and relief; Order 8 prescribes what must be in the written statement including specific denials; together they define the pleading stage that frames the issues for trial.

queries.query: How do Sections 2 and 96 define what is appealable as a decree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Section 2 defines a decree as a formal adjudication conclusively determining rights; Section 96 provides for appeal from every decree; only decrees are appealable under Section 96 and not orders.

queries.query: How do Orders 22 and 23 relate to abatement and withdrawal of suits?
